must_identify.text: The five detections are presented as one persistence chain on corpws58, oldest to newest: WINWORD.EXE spawns hidden PowerShell, PowerShell writes C:\ProgramData\WinSvcCache\svcupd.exe, PowerShell sets a Run key value to that file, a service WinSvcCache is installed with that image and auto start, and services.exe starts svcupd.exe.
The brief names two persistence mechanisms for the same binary: the Run key value (T1547.001) and the auto-start service (T1543.003).
The new corpws58:9443/tcp listener from the recon delta is tied to the chain as corroboration, and the brief requests the process that owns the port instead of asserting that svcupd.exe holds it.

Confidence is High, justified by the detections plus the recon change as independent corroboration and by the absence of a plausible benign reading of an Office document installing an auto-start binary under ProgramData.

Options include isolating corpws58 as a containment option with its trade-off, collecting svcupd.exe and shipping-notice-0816.docm before the Run key value and the WinSvcCache service are removed, and searching other hosts for the svcupd.exe hash, its path or dl.media-share.test.

must_not.text: The brief does not discount the file-write detection (rule 100938, level 7) as noise or as below threshold; it is in the intake because the include list names it, and it links PowerShell to svcupd.exe.
The brief does not state as fact what svcupd.exe does or what serves 9443/tcp (its capabilities, a C2 address, a malware family); the intake shows neither.
